caption_instagram:
The driver fled? You still have rights after a road accident. 🚑

🏥 Cashless treatment up to ₹1.5 lakh per victim, for up to 7 days from the accident (Cashless Treatment of Road Accident Victims Scheme, 2025)
🚗 Hit-and-run: ₹2 lakh compensation on death, ₹50,000 for grievous injury (2022 scheme)
🤝 Good Samaritans who help victims are protected from civil or criminal liability and need not share their identity (MV Act s.134A)
⚖️ A compensation claim can be filed before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal where the accident happened or where you live
🆘 In an emergency, call 112

caption_linkedin:
Many families facing a road accident don't know what support the law already provides. Four points worth sharing:

• Cashless treatment: under the Cashless Treatment of Road Accident Victims Scheme, 2025, a victim of a motor vehicle accident can get cashless treatment of up to ₹1.5 lakh, for up to seven days from the date of the accident.
• Hit-and-run: under the 2022 compensation scheme for hit-and-run motor accidents, ₹2 lakh is payable on death and ₹50,000 for grievous hurt — even when the vehicle is never traced.
• Good Samaritans: Section 134A of the Motor Vehicles Act protects people who help accident victims in good faith from civil or criminal liability, and they cannot be compelled to disclose their identity.
• Claims: under Section 166(2), a compensation claim can be filed before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal where the accident occurred, where the claimant resides or carries on business, or where the defendant resides.

For guidance on accident claims, you can consult a Bar Council-verified advocate online on AdvocateSetu: https://advocatesetu.com
